articles.title: Food delivery startup Wonder files for IPO as it explores its next big bite | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Following years of fundraising, acquisitions, and expansion, food delivery startup Wonder is moving closer to becoming a publicly traded company.
articles.body_text: Food delivery startup Wonder is moving closer to becoming a publicly traded company after confidentially filing for an initial public offering (IPO). The company announced the filing on Thursday, marking a major milestone following years of fundraising, acquisitions, and expansion. Wonder has yet to reveal how many shares it plans to make available or the expected price range. Founded in 2018 by entrepreneur Marc Lore, Wonder has evolved from a food delivery concept into a broader food technology business. Its model goes beyond traditional delivery apps, with the company operating food hall-style locations where customers can order meals from multiple restaurant brands through a single platform. The company handles everything from meal preparation to delivery, pickup, and dine-in service. Lore, who previously founded Jet.com and Diapers.com, has made no secret of his plans to take Wonder public. Those ambitions gained further attention in July, when the company announced it had raised more than $650 million in a funding round that valued it at around $9 billion. Investors include Accel, GV, AllianceBernstein, and ARK Invest. Meanwhile, Wonder has been busy expanding its footprint and strengthening its business through acquisitions. The company has outlined ambitious growth plans, including a major push into Texas, where it aims to open more than 100 locations by the end of 2027. Additionally, Wonder has acquired meal-kit company Blue Apron , restaurant delivery platform Grubhub , media company Tastemade , and kitchen robotics company Spyce. The latter acquisition gives Wonder access to automation technology that could help streamline food preparation and improve how food is served. Wonder is also branching out with Wonder Create , its platform focused on letting food entrepreneurs and social media influencers develop new food concepts, restaurant brands, and menu items. The platform leverages AI to design and launch restaurant brands in less than a minute. Another notable move is its $425 million partnership with DoorDash to expand its campus dining business, which operates at 450 colleges and universities and other locations. Despite its growth, a move into the public markets will bring new challenges. Wonder is operating in an increasingly competitive food delivery landscape, going up against established names such as DoorDash and Uber Eats. articles.title: Axiom Math wants to keep AI slop out of mathematics | TechCrunch
articles.summary: As AI floods math with unchecked proofs, Axiom Math is betting on verification. The startup’s AI agents just formally verified the Stacks Project, one of the field’s biggest libraries.
articles.body_text: It feels like AI is cracking a new math problem every week. Last month, OpenAI released 719 manuscripts claiming solutions to some of the field’s hardest problems. But even the computer checks meant to confirm those results can slip . After years of AI slop, it’s fair to wonder whether math is next. Axiom Math is betting math can avoid that fate, not by slowing down, but by standing on firmer ground. The $1.6 billion startup wants to build a verified foundation that AI agents can rely on to write software and, eventually, do science. On Wednesday, the company announced it had formally verified the Stacks Project, one of the largest bodies of mathematics ever written by humans. Mathematicians often hold Stacks in rare regard — Columbia mathematician Peter Woit has claimed there’s “ nothing else really comparable ,” comparing the project to “ the famous Bourbaki books ,” a series that rebuilt math from its foundations in the 20th century. Woit’s Columbia colleague Johan de Jong started the Stacks Project in 2005 as an open source reference. Mathematicians have contributed to it ever since, building out results from college-level algebra all the way up to the field’s most advanced ideas across algebra, geometry, and number theory. The company’s fleet of AI agents translates the library’s roughly 7,654 pages into about 16 million lines of computer-checked code. Formalizing math is a way of making sure the structure underneath it is sound. Mathematicians rewrite the proof as code in a programming language called Lean, and a program called a proof assistant checks the code line by line. If the proof passes, mathematicians can trust that it’s logically sound. Engineers use the same idea, called formal verification, to confirm their chip designs work , while researchers in France have used it to catch bugs in software that calculates family benefits. For a library like the Stacks Project, checking each theorem is only part of the job. The theorems and definitions in Stacks are interconnected, and each one builds on the ones before it. Like a family tree, many results in Stacks trace back to the ones that came before it. That interconnectedness made Axiom unsure the project would work at first. The team had to keep every connection intact across about 16 million lines of Lean code. “Things that are big and things that are delicate in life just don’t go together,” Axiom CEO Carina Hong told TechCrunch. “[Stacks] is a collection of mathematical results that is the foundation of mathematics. You want [theorems] to be consistent and not, like, paradoxical. You want the definitions to not fight with each other.” The 25-year-old CEO dropped out of a Stanford math PhD program and founded the company in March 2025. In March, Axiom raised a $200 million Series A led by Menlo Ventures . “We were not sure if vibe coding would be able to preserve the beauty of Stacks,” Hong said.

articles.title: A YC startup is putting $1M behind 5 unsolved materials science problems for AI | TechCrunch
articles.summary: While frontier AI models have solved a remarkable series of outstanding mathematics problems and made progress in the life sciences, they have yet to truly plumb the complex physics in advanced materials.
articles.body_text: Discovered Materials, a months-old San Francisco startup using AI models to find new substances for building advanced chips, announced a million-dollar challenge for AI models to solve five critical problems in materials science. While frontier AI models have solved a remarkable series of outstanding mathematics problems and made progress in the life sciences, they have yet to truly plumb the complex physics in advanced materials. “It’s more difficult to specify problems clearly in materials science because it’s not like math, where you have a very specific definition and can get to a yes or no,” said Advaith Sridhar, a co-founder of Discovered Materials, which was part of Y Combinator’s spring 2026 batch. “We came to this discussion [wondering], what are the grand challenges in this field? How do we know AI is making progress?” Though materials science doesn’t have an equivalent of the Millennium Prize Problems, Discovered Materials recruited an advisory group of academics at leading global universities to spell out five open problems. The company is offering a pool of prizes, worth $1 million in total, for solutions to the problems. “Across materials science, there are phenomena we observe but cannot explain,” Felipe Jornada, a Stanford professor who helped develop the challenges, said in a statement. “Explaining these phenomena would improve our understanding of physics, and the answers would directly shape how we build electronics, store energy, and manufacture the materials of the future.” Before announcing the challenges, Discovered Materials turned frontier lab models loose on them, giving AI agents internet access and other resources to work autonomously for days. The models spent several days on each problem without making much headway. Still, it’s easy to imagine OpenAI or Anthropic attempting to one-shot them with significantly more compute or a newer model. “It’s not particularly a concern to us whether we find it, or someone else finds it, or a professor finds it, or the frontier labs find it,” Sridhar said. “The reason we’re putting out these challenges is because we want them to serve as the goalposts. If you go and solve these challenges, we are deepening our understanding of materials and how things around us behave.” Tracking efforts to solve the problems will show “whether the models are climbing in this domain,” he added. The challenge also reflects the changing nature of scientific inquiry as AI proves capable of uncovering insights and techniques human researchers didn’t anticipate. With solutions apparently easier to find than ever, the questions become more important. “This is a new way of thinking about science, where we come up with the verification and the challenges first, and then we let somebody come up with the ideas that explain the problem,” Sridhar said. “Knowing what are the right questions to ask is not trivial and very difficult in this domain, so this is where the professors have really helped us shape what are the right questions we should be asking.” Discovered Materials’ main focus is developing new materials for use in semiconductors; the startup partners with chip giants on research projects while also funding its own scientific efforts. When the company announced its seed round in August, Sridhar told TechCrunch that he hoped the company would generate a useful material within a year. “Those timelines have accelerated a little bit,” he says today. “I’m more confident now that we will be able to find these industrially useful materials in a timeline shorter than a year.”

articles.summary: Trump pressas av sina egna rådgivare att sparka krigsminister Pete Hegseth. ”De vädrar blod”, säger en tjänsteman i regeringen.
articles.body_text: Trump pressas av sina egna rådgivare att sparka krigsminister Pete Hegseth. – De vädrar blod, säger en tjänsteman i regeringen till MS NOW . Trump överväger att ersätta Hegseth, enligt NBC News. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Pete Hegseths tid som USA:s krigsminister har varit turbulent. Han delade förra året uppgifter om planerade amerikanska attacker i en Signal-chatt där en journalist av misstag var inbjuden. Hegseth var också en av arkitekterna bakom attackerna mot Iran. Vicepresident JD Vance skyllde republikanernas katastrofala mellanårsresultat på Irankriget. På en fråga om presidenten höll med Vance svarade Trump: – Det är till stor del sant eftersom det drev upp bensinpriset lite. Men om jag var tvungen att göra det igen så skulle jag göra det igen. Hegseth står inför hot om riksrätt från både republikaner och demokrater när kongressen återvänder nästa vecka. Republikanske representanthusledamoten Thomas Massie har sagt att han avser att tvinga fram en omröstning om Hegseth i kongressen nästa vecka om Pentagonchefen inte avgår innan dess. Nu har Donald Trump frågat sina närmaste vad de tycker om krigsminister Pete Hegseth, enligt MS Now. Vissa rådgivare pressar presidenten att ersätta Pentagonchefen, enligt två tjänstemän i regeringen. – Det finns många människor som vill ha hans skalp och de vädrar blod. De pressar Trump. Alla vet att Trump kommer att vilja ha någon att skylla på, säger en tjänsteman. NBC News rapporterade på torsdagen att Trump har berättat för några av sina närmaste att han överväger att ersätta Hegseth. På en fråga av ABC News om han skulle ersätta Hegseth svarade Trump dock att han har för ”avsikt att behålla honom”. – Jag får de här samtalen om honom. Jag förstår inte varför, säger Trump.

articles.title: Vägrade lägga ananas på pizza – fick sparken
articles.summary: Kocken Davide Tamburella vägrade ha ananas på pizzorna. Han betraktade det som en ”en förolämpning mot hans kultur”. Det ledde till att han fick sparken.
articles.body_text: Kocken Davide Tamburella vägrade ha ananas på pizzorna. Han betraktade det som en ”en förolämpning mot hans kultur”. Det ledde till att han fick sparken, skriver Guardian . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Davide Tamburella var kock på en restaurang i Australien som utlovade ”klassiska italienska rätter”. Men italienaren fick sparken i somras, två veckor efter att hans chef pratat med honom om ”farhågor kring hans arbetsprestationer”. Bland dessa fanns Tamburellas vägran att ha ananas på pizza med motiveringen att det var ”en förolämpning mot hans kultur”. Tamburella ska flera gånger ha vägrat göra en hawaii och i stället uppmanat chefen att ”kontrollera hur viktigt det är för italienare att inte ha ananas på en pizza”. Chefen pratade om vikten av ”välja sina strider”. – Skulle jag själv köpa en skinka- och ananaspizza? Det är nog inte min absoluta favorit. Men jag tänker inte rynka på näsan åt det heller, säger chefen. När uppsägningen togs upp i en arbetsdomstol i veckan framkom det att uppsägningen ställde till det rejält för Tamburella. Han har i över tre år genomgått en ansökningsprocess för att få ett permanent uppehållstillstånd i Australien. Men processen kräver fast anställning – och när han fick sparken fick han börja om igen med en ny ansökan. Italienaren hävdade att han sparkades på felaktiga grunder men fick avslag. Tamburella är nu anställd på en annan italiensk restaurang. Pizza med ananas ska inte finnas med på menyn. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. articles.title: Fick sju miljoner på kroken: Överlycklig
articles.summary: Matthew Maurice fick napp. Det blev 26-åringen sju miljoner kronor rikare på. ”De två mest stressiga minuterna i mitt liv”, säger Matthew.
articles.body_text: Det blev 26-åringen sju miljoner kronor rikare på. – Det var förmodligen de två mest stressiga minuterna i mitt liv, säger Matthew till australiska 7News. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. 26-årige australiern Matthew Maurice ville umgås med sin bror som var på besök förra veckan. Syskonen begav sig därför ut med en båt för att fiska vid Corroboree Billabong. – Vi orkade inte ta oss ut så långt så vi åkte bara mindre än en kilometer från båtrampen. Vi ville bara fiska och prata, det var allt. Om vi ​​fick napp eller inte spelade ingen roll, vi ville bara vara tillsammans, säger Matthew. Men visst fick Matthew napp – och inte vilket napp som helst. Han fick en 80 centimeter lång barramundi, en stor rovfisk som finns i Australien och Sydostasien, på kroken. Men mest intressant var att fisken hade en röd märkning fäst på sig. – Jag såg fisken hoppa inom de första tio sekunderna och fick syn på en knallröd tagg som hängde ut från den. Det var förmodligen de två mest stressiga minuterna i mitt liv, säger Matthew. Han lyckades håva upp fisken vars märkning innebar att Maurice hade vunnit en miljon dollar, motsvarande 6,8 miljoner kronor. Det var nämligen topp-priset i en regional fisketävling för att öka turismen där vissa fiskar på förhand märkts med olika belopp och sedan släppts ut för att fiskare ska försöka fånga dem. Det är bara andra gången i tävlingens tolvåriga historia som någon faktiskt fångat en barramundi värd en miljon dollar. – Jag var bara glad att få napp. Jag kan inte fatta att jag fick upp en fisk värd en miljon dollar, säger Matthew. Maurice ringde sin mamma först för att berätta om de goda nyheterna och sade: Han planerar att använda pengarna till att köpa ett hus och ”unna sig något gott”. – Jag är överlycklig. Det är bara en känslostorm just nu, säger Matthew.
